articles.title: Minimally Invasive Zadek Osteotomy vs Open Achilles Debridement for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy in Athletes: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Genuth G, Stavrou P, Brown C, Iselin LD
articles.population: Athletic patients with insertional Achilles tendinopathy who failed at least 6 months of conservative treatment
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (25 minimally invasive Zadek osteotomy, 25 open surgery)
articles.outcomes: Time to return to sport, return-to-sport rate, patient-reported physical function and pain, postoperative complications
articles.take_home: Minimally invasive Zadek osteotomy allowed athletes to return to sport about 1.8 months faster than traditional open surgery (4.3 versus 6.1 months) with better early recovery and fewer complications. By 18 months, both groups had similar overall improvements in function and pain.

articles.title: Lambrinudi-Type Arthrodesis and Plantar Fasciectomy in the Treatment of Rigid Cavovarus Deformity.
articles.authors: Ruiz R, Susdorf R, Hintermann B
articles.population: Patients with rigid cavovarus deformity (neurogenic and non-neurogenic)
articles.outcomes: Pain reduction (VAS scale decreased by 6.5 points), function improvement (EFAS score increased by 31.5 points), radiographic measurements improved, foot length increased by 10.1%
articles.take_home: A Lambrinudi-type arthrodesis combined with plantar fasciectomy significantly reduced pain and improved function in patients with rigid cavovarus deformity, with similar results in both neurogenic and non-neurogenic feet. The procedure corrected foot shape and increased foot length by approximately 10 percent.

articles.title: Early clinical outcomes following eccentric loading versus manual fascial release in mid-portion achilles tendinopathy: A retrospective observational study.
articles.authors: Xia H, Wei Q, Bai H, Huang S, Dong G, Sun Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients with mid-portion Achilles tendon pain lasting 4 weeks or longer
articles.sample_size: 60 patients (20 in each of three groups)
articles.outcomes: VISA-A score, FAAM score, heel-rise height, triple-hop distance
articles.take_home: At 6 weeks, manual fascial release reduced symptoms faster whilst eccentric training improved function faster, but by 12 weeks both active treatments produced similar results. The study cannot confirm which technique is genuinely better because patients were not randomly allocated and there was no sham treatment control.

articles.title: Mid-term clinical outcomes of combined forefoot surgery including minimally invasive hammertoe correction.
articles.authors: Pochgraber P, Stumpner T, Bischofreiter M, Katzensteiner M, Bock P
articles.population: Patients with hammertoe deformity, with or without hallux valgus, undergoing minimally invasive correction
articles.outcomes: European Foot and Ankle Society score, American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society score, Foot Function Index, visual analogue scale pain score, and radiographic union
articles.take_home: Minimally invasive hammertoe surgery improved pain scores significantly, with pain reducing from 5.62 to 0.86 on a visual scale and all toes healing properly at 30 months follow-up. Patients also showed meaningful improvements in foot function and quality of life scores after the procedure.

articles.title: EFAS Score Validation of the Slovak Version by the Score Committee of the European Foot and Ankle Society (EFAS).
articles.authors: Richter M, Agren PH, Besse JL, Coester M, Kofoed H, Maffulli N, et al.
articles.population: Patients with foot and ankle pathologies undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Internal consistency, measurement error, responsiveness to change in EFAS Score Slovak version
articles.take_home: The Slovak version of the EFAS Score has been validated and works reliably to measure outcomes in foot and ankle patients, with 81 percent of patients showing improvement after surgery.
